checks: The sampled bases are finite by compactness. The convex hull of the lifts has the same fibers at sampled bases by both inclusions; any integer point in the convex hull of sampled bases lies in the convex projection of C and is sampled.

M>0 gives an interior point in a positive fiber, of positive depth. Each halfspace containing the chosen interior segment point contains at least one endpoint by affinity of its margin. Its mass is at least Q, so the sampled segment point has depth Q and maximizes on its own positive fiber.

The accepted critical-circuit theorem supplies actual nonvertical through-y caps of mass Q and a minimal positive dependence of unit continuous normals with 2≤s≤d+1. If the minimal normal set were affinely dependent, one could perturb the strictly positive normalized coefficients along an affine dependence until one coefficient first vanished, retaining a convex representation of zero with smaller support. Thus the affine hull has dimension s−1, contains zero, and equals the linear span.

For each circuit cap, the interpolation lemma's assumption D(y)=min(D(y_0),D(y_1)) holds. Each cap already exists and attains the depth at y. Both endpoint margins vanish and the cap attains their depths; positive depth puts each endpoint in its positive fiber interior.

Dropping null fibers in the flux step preserves μ and does not remove either endpoint. The chosen ambient h, common cap property and normalized continuous normals match the flux hypotheses. Apply the individual inequality with full-side term +∫(1+δ) and empty-side term +∫δ on its right. Positive λ_i preserve the inequalities on addition. Since A_i>0, each empty-side exterior integral is positive, so a section of positive weighted measure exists in the finite family.

A positive (d−1)-measure supporting face of a full-dimensional polytope has dimension exactly d−1 and is a facet, including a supporting endpoint in dimension one. No same-base shear is used. For distinct bases the translation has affine inverse and preserves volume on each fiber. The two transformed endpoint continuous coordinates are zero; subtraction of their affine margins yields a'_i·(p_1−p_0)=0, and the continuous normal is unchanged.

Original e81d0f726880ea4a §2 (4) provides the oriented circuit sum. Original f2d1fbdd5a877f5b §4 gives the balanced circuit and distinct-base shear (4). The normalized source masses βμ(S) correspond to raw Q. The revised proof supplies a fiberwise circuit in place of the original cover argument and keeps distinct bases only for the shear. Both raw source digests match.
